title: Henry IV, Part 1
author: William Shakespeare
openingChapterLabel: Act 1, Scene 1 — London. A Room in the Palace
openingText: King Henry, still shaken by the civil wars that put him on the throne, hears that the young rebel Hotspur has won a great victory in the north — and wishes Hotspur were his son instead of the tavern-loving Prince Hal.
about:
Henry IV, Part 1 opens a year after Henry Bolingbroke took the crown from Richard II. The new king wants peace and a crusade, but his throne is shaky. The Percy family, who helped him to power, feel cheated and turn against him, led by the fiery young Hotspur. Meanwhile the king's own son, Prince Hal, spends his days in the taverns of Eastcheap with Sir John Falstaff, a fat, witty, cowardly and endlessly inventive old knight.

The play moves between court, rebel camp and tavern. Hal and Poins trick Falstaff after a highway robbery; Falstaff and Hal take turns playing the king; Hotspur quarrels with his allies over a map of England. Everything leads to the battle of Shrewsbury, where Hal finally steps forward, saves his father and faces Hotspur in single combat, while Falstaff gives his famous verdict on honour.

Shakespeare wrote the play around 1597. Falstaff became one of his most popular characters, and the story continues in Henry IV, Part 2 and Henry V.

whyItMatters.title: Growing up in public
whyItMatters.body: Hal knows everyone thinks he is a waster, and he plans to surprise them. The play asks whether his tavern years are a disguise, a real friendship, or both. Readers who have felt judged too early will recognize the question.

whyItMatters.title: Falstaff
whyItMatters.body: Falstaff lies, steals, boasts and runs away, and he is still the most alive person in the play. His speech on honour asks what a word is worth if it cannot save a life. Many readers come away siding with him.

whyItMatters.title: Three ideas of honour
whyItMatters.body: Hotspur lives for glory, Falstaff laughs at it, and Hal learns to use it. Watching the three side by side shows how one idea can drive war, comedy and politics at once.

angleCards.title: Hal's plan
angleCards.text: From his first speech Hal says he will reform at the right moment. Track whether you believe him.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to follow Prince Hal and decide whether his wild youth is a calculated act or a real life he gives up.

angleCards.title: Falstaff on trial
angleCards.text: Count Falstaff's lies and escapes, and notice when the jokes turn serious.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to read Falstaff closely and decide what the play wants us to think of him.

angleCards.title: Hotspur and Hal
angleCards.text: The two Harrys are set up as mirror images. Compare how each speaks, fights and treats others.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to compare Hotspur and Hal as two models of a young nobleman.

angleCards.title: Court and tavern
angleCards.text: Notice how the scenes alternate and how the tavern parodies the court.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to see how the comic and political plots comment on each other.

cast.name: King Henry IV
cast.description: Once Henry Bolingbroke, who took the crown from Richard II. He longs for peace and a crusade but faces rebellion from the family that helped him rise, and despairs of his son.

cast.name: Prince Hal
cast.description: Henry's eldest son, who spends his time with Falstaff in Eastcheap. He promises himself he will one day surprise the world, and at Shrewsbury he does.

cast.name: Sir John Falstaff
cast.description: An old, fat, witty knight, Hal's drinking companion: a liar, thief and coward who talks his way out of everything.

cast.name: Hotspur
cast.description: Henry Percy, son of the Earl of Northumberland. Brave, impatient and obsessed with honour, he leads the rebellion against the king.

cast.name: Worcester and Northumberland
cast.description: Hotspur's uncle and father, who helped Henry to the throne and now plot against him.

cast.name: Glendower
cast.description: Owen Glendower, the Welsh rebel leader who claims magical powers; he and Hotspur clash constantly.
